message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (`code.exe`) from the command line** On Windows you can stop VS Code (and its renderer/worker children) with `taskkill`. Below are the most common ways to do it: | What you want to do | Command | Notes | |---------------------|---------|-------| | **Kill all running VS Code windows** (forcefully, including child processes) | ```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
``` | `/IM` matches the image name (`code.exe`).
`/F` forces termination.
`/T` also terminates any child processes launched by the main `code.exe`. | | **Kill a specific instance by PID** | ```cmd
taskkill /PID /F
``` | Replace `` with the number shown by `tasklist`. | | **Find the PID(s) of VS Code** | ```cmd
tasklist | findstr /I code.exe
``` | Shows all `code.exe` processes and their PIDs. | | **PowerShell alternative** | ```powershell
Stop-Process -Name code -Force
``` | Equivalent to `taskkill /IM code.exe /F`. | ### Quick one‑liner If you just want to close *all* VS Code windows immediately: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T ``` That will terminate the main `code.exe` process and any renderer/worker processes it spawned. --- #### Why `/T` matters VS Code launches several helper processes (`code.exe`, `code.exe (renderer)`, etc.). Without `/T`, only the top‑level `code.exe` would be killed; the helpers might keep running until they exit on their own. Adding `/T` ensures the whole tree is shut down. --- #### Common pitfalls | Problem | Fix | |---------|-----| | “Access denied” error | Run the command prompt as Administrator, or add `/FI "USERNAME eq "` to target only your user’s processes. | | “No tasks found” | Make sure VS Code is actually running. Check with `tasklist | findstr code.exe`. | | Multiple instances | If you only want to close a particular window, first get its PID (`tasklist | findstr code.exe`) then use `/PID `. | Feel free to copy/paste the commands above into a normal CMD window or a PowerShell prompt. Happy coding!
